messages:
Maya N.: FYI flagged a FinSage escalation — they say replies are suddenly more 'jargon-heavy' and shorter after the model bump yesterday. They included side-by-side examples.
FinSage Support: Customer says responses now 'skip small talk' and use denser technical terms (e.g., 'quantize-aware kernels' instead of 'reduce precision'). Example: \n-- before (v4.9): \"You can lower costs by using int8 quantization; here's a short guide...\"\n-- after (v5.0): \"Apply int8 quantization for throughput; refer to kernel fusion docs.\" They want this rolled back or mitigated.
Samir K.: Thanks. Do we have deployment metadata? Which variant/region did they hit?
DeployBot: Deployed redwood-v5.0 to prod-west, prod-eu at 2026-03-14T04:12:32Z (rollout 100%).
Maya N.: Customer's request id: req_0a1b2c3d; attached transcript and API payload. They hit prod-west.
FinSage Support: Added repro steps: \n1) POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-v5.0 and system prompt: \"You are a senior infra engineer. Be concise and technical.\" \n2) user prompt: \"How do I reduce inference cost for LLMs?\" \n3) compare tokens and tone.
Elaine Z.: Hmm they have a system prompt that explicitly instructs conciseness/technical voice. Can we reproduce without that prompt? Might be prompt amplification + model policy tweak.
Samir K.: Repro checklist I need: (1) raw request body, (2) deterministic seed or temperature, (3) model+revision. Also want mean token length and top-1 phrase overlap metrics for v4.9 vs v5.0.
Maya N.: Pasting customer's raw body: ```{\n  "model": "redwood-v5.0",\n  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are a senior infra engineer. Be concise and technical."},{"role":"user","content":"How do I reduce inference cost for LLMs?"}],\n  "temperature": 0.0\n}```
Samir K.: Thanks. I'll run a quick side-by-side with v4.9 and v5.0. Hypothesis: a training-time objective tweak sharpened token selection and the new default system-prompt handling compresses framing. Could be an instruction-following regression (shorter, more jargon). I'll check generation length distribution and logprob deltas for the example ID.
FinSage Support: Customer notes it's not just length — phrasing changed (more acronyms, fewer explanation sentences). They rely on user-facing wording for non-expert customers; this regression impacts UX.
Elaine Z.: If it's instruction-following shift, we can ship a soft fallback policy: route tiered requests from that customer to v4.9 (compatible) for 48h while we investigate. Any objections?
Samir K.: No objections. Need support auth to enable routing policy. Also will instrument an eval: run a small prompt-suite and compute readability score (Flesch) + jargon token ratio.
Maya N.: Created an interim routing ticket and requested customer opt-in for traffic mirroring. Ticket ID: SUP-4287. @FinSage Support can you confirm they can try mirrored traffic? :thumbsup:
FinSage Support: They've agreed to mirrored tests and would like a rollback if mirroring shows significant quality drop.
Samir K.: I'll attach repro artifacts and results here once I have numbers (should have initial run in ~2h). Short-term plan: mirror -> metric check (length, jargon ratio, readability) -> decide rollback or soft-prompt shim.
Maya N.: Great. Also putting a note to docs team: add guidance for customers who surface-model-verbosity changes after upgrades (how to test with prompt shims and routing).
Samir K.: Update: initial run shows average response length dropped 18% and jargon token ratio up ~12% for the customer's prompt set. Pushing more detailed diff shortly. Suggest temporary route of FinSage to redwood-v4.9 in prod-west while we validate fixes.
Elaine Z.: I'll draft the routing change and coordinate with SRE for the 24–48h window. Thanks everyone.
FinSage Support: Appreciated. We'll keep the customer posted.
